answer: Behavioral ridge clustering. After transactions settle, fit each identity's action history to an agent-behavior model and cluster residuals; identities whose residual vectors sit on a shared low-variance ridge are flagged as one operator. Enforcement marks the whole ridge and freezes payouts held in the vault pending review. An attacker must spend per identity to buy distinct, noisy histories that dodge the ridge fit, and each flagged cluster forfeits accumulated balances and its harbor of repeat counterparties.
